==Ever Grande City (North)==
[[File:Ever Grande City League Lobby RS.png|thumb|Pokémon League, Lobby]]
===The Pokémon League===
The {{ho|Pokémon League}} building holds the traditional amenities, with a Pokémon Center and PC to the left, and a Poké Mart to the right. It's a good idea to stock up on items that restore health and status ailments for the gauntlet ahead.

With your preparations complete, speak to the two Cooltrainers guarding the doorway in the room's center. They verify that you've earned all eight [[Hoenn League]] Badges before stepping aside, allowing you to enter the depths of the Pokémon League. Challengers must face the [[Elite Four]] and {{pkmn|Champion}} in quick succession, with no outside help.

====Elite Four====
[[File:Sidney room RSE.png|thumb|Elite Four (1): Sidney's room]]
=====Battle 1=====
The first member of the Elite Four is [[Sidney]], a master of {{type|Dark}} Pokémon. Dark-type moves are super effective against {{t|Ghost}}- and {{type|Psychic}} Pokémon, while Dark-type Pokémon are weak to {{t|Bug}}- and {{type|Fighting}} moves, and immune to Psychic-type moves.

Sidney leads with his {{p|Mightyena}}, which immediately cuts the opponent's physical {{stat|Attack}} with its {{a|Intimidate}} Ability. Use [[special move]]s to bypass this stat drop. {{p|Cacturne}}'s {{m|Leech Seed}} steals the target's health for its own, and {{m|Cotton Spore}} cuts the target's {{stat|Speed}}. As a {{2t|Grass|Dark}} Pokémon, it takes massive damage from {{type|Bug}} moves. His {{p|Shiftry}} can {{m|Extrasensory}} to retaliate against {{type|Fighting}} Pokémon, but it falters against {{t|Fire}}, {{t|Ice}}, and {{t|Flying}} moves. {{p|Sharpedo}} can be dangerous due to its high physical {{stat|Attack}} and Speed, but it is rather fragile and cannot sustain much damage. Beware of its {{a|Rough Skin}} Ability! Finally, his {{p|Absol}}'s high physical Attack lets it hit hard with any attack, and {{m|Swords Dance}} lets it deal even more damage. {{m|Aerial Ace}} is a sure-hit move meant to deter Fighting Pokémon. Its defenses are mediocre, so use your strongest moves to keep up the pressure and take it down.

[[File:Phoebe room RSE.png|thumb|Elite Four (2): Phoebe's room]]
=====Battle 2=====
The second member of the Elite Four is [[Phoebe]], a master of {{type|Ghost}} Pokémon. Ghost-type moves are super effective against Ghost- and {{type|Psychic}} Pokémon, while Ghost-type Pokémon are weak to {{t|Dark}}- and Ghost-type moves, and immune to {{t|Normal}}- and {{type|Fighting}} moves.

[[Phoebe]] leads with the first of her two {{p|Dusclops}}. A defensive-oriented Pokémon, it is more interested in causing status ailments than attacking. Weaken its defenses, or boost your Pokémon's offenses, before attacking with super effective moves. Next up are her two {{p|Banette}}; the first can trigger a {{status|burn}} with {{m|Will-O-Wisp}}, and the second can induce {{stat|Poison|poisoning}} with {{m|Toxic}}. Both can use {{m|Shadow Ball}} as well, which may cut the target's {{stat|Special Defense}}. Due to its unique {{2t|Dark|Ghost}} typing, her {{p|Sableye}} has no weaknesses under normal conditions; however, using {{m|Foresight}} exposes its Dark-type vulnerability to {{t|Fighting}} moves. Most of its moves deal damage, while {{m|Attract}} hinders male targets. Finally, her second Dusclops has a more varied moveset, which lets it deal serious damage to a wider variety of targets. Use the same strategies as before to defeat this one, as well.

[[File:Glacia room RSE.png|thumb|Elite Four (3): Glacia's room]]
=====Battle 3=====
The third member of the Elite Four is [[Glacia]], a master of {{type|Ice}} Pokémon. Ice-type moves are super effective against {{t|Dragon}}-, {{t|Flying}}-, {{t|Grass}}-, and {{type|Ground}} Pokémon, while Ice-type Pokémon are weak to {{t|Fighting}}-, {{t|Fire}}-, {{t|Rock}}-, and {{type|Steel}} moves.

[[Glacia]] leads with the first of her two {{p|Glalie}}. {{m|Hail}} inflicts residual damage to all non-{{t|Ice}} Pokémon for five turns, and increases {{m|Blizzard}}'s accuracy to 100%. {{m|Light Screen}} temporarily reduces the damage her team takes from [[special move]]s, so attacks like {{m|Flamethrower}} are less effective. Use {{t|Rock}} and {{t|Fighting}} moves to bring it down. Next, the first of her two {{p|Sealeo}}. Like Glalie, it can also trigger a [[Hail (weather condition)|hailstorm]], and has {{t|Water}} and Ice attacks to back it up. Avoid using {{t|Fire}} attacks, as its {{a|Thick Fat}} Ability weakens such moves. Her second Sealeo is much the same as the first, but carries the powerful Blizzard attack, and can disrupt male targets with {{m|Attract}}. Her second Glalie has a more varied moveset, which lets it deal serious damage to a wider variety of targets. Finally, her {{p|Walrein}} has powerful attacks in Blizzard and {{m|Surf}}, and is especially dangerous to lower-leveled opponents because of {{m|Sheer Cold}}.

[[File:Drake room RSE.png|thumb|Elite Four (4): Drake's room]]
=====Battle 4=====
The final member of the Elite Four is [[Drake]], a master of {{type|Dragon}} Pokémon. Dragon-type moves are super effective against Dragon-type Pokémon, while Dragon-type Pokémon are weak to Dragon- and {{type|Ice}} moves.

[[Drake]] leads with his {{p|Shelgon}}. Its strongest move is {{m|Dragon Claw}}. {{m|Rock Tomb}} helps the sluggish Pokémon even the playing field by cutting the target's {{stat|Speed}}; it also lets it retaliate against {{type|Ice}} Pokémon. Next up, his {{p|Altaria}} can boost its physical {{stat|Attack}} and Speed with {{m|Dragon Dance}}, which pairs well with {{m|Take Down}}. Avoid inflicting status ailments, as both {{m|Refresh}} and its {{a|Natural Cure}} Ability allow it to restore itself. Drake's team includes a pair of {{p|Flygon}}; the first uses [[special move]]s, and the second relies on [[physical move]]s. Both are vulnerable to {{t|Water}} moves, and take massive damage from Ice attacks. Finally, his {{p|Salamence}} has high offenses and Speed, and {{a|Intimidate}} cuts the target's physical Attack. Use special moves, like {{m|Ice Beam}}, to bring it down.

With the Elite Four defeated, you have earned the right to challenge the reigning Champion of the [[Hoenn]] region. Be sure to make any preparations before entering the final room, as you will be drawn into battle almost immediately.

[[File:Champion Steven room RS.png|thumb|Champion's room]]
====Champion====
Inside the Champion's hall, you find your mentor [[Steven Stone|Steven]] waiting for you. He is curious to know how much you've learned in your travels, and asks that you battle him with all your might. He promises to do the same with his Pokémon, as well. The stage is set for a legendary showdown! His Pokémon are of many different types, and don't share as many weaknesses as the Elite Four's teams. However, he still prefers his beloved {{t|Steel}} Pokémon, and most of his Pokémon belong to either the {{t|Rock}} or {{t|Ground}} types as well—no surprise from this well-known stone collector. With such a varied team, be sure to switch out your Pokémon as needed to capitalize on his Pokémon's weaknesses. Use your best strategies and your strongest attacks to bring down the Champion!

With the battle concluded, [[Steven Stone|Steven]] congratulates you on your impressive victory. Just as he is about to crown you the new Hoenn League Champion, {{ga|May}}/{{ga|Brendan}} rushes in with some advice—only to find that you've already won. [[Professor Birch]] arrives a moment later, impressed that you have defeated not only [[Norman|your father]], but the Champion as well. He rates your Pokédex progress before congratulating you as well.

====Hall of Fame====
[[Steven Stone|Steven]] leads you into the [[Hall of Fame]] room, where all victorious Pokémon and thier Champions are honored. Once you set your Pokémon on the machine here, the details of both you and your party members are recorded. During the process, a shot of each Pokémon appears briefly on-screen. The screen fades to black, and the game is saved.
